docRequirement: env-vars.md:425 binds the subagent-output cap to `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`: "Maximum number of characters in subagent output before truncation (default: 32000, maximum: 160000). When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response". Three obligations: the cap counts CHARACTERS, it is user-tunable via that env var between the default 32000 and a 160000 maximum, and a truncated response must name the on-disk file holding the full output.
current: Truncation exists and is live, but as a fixed byte cut with no spill and no knob. `OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES = 32 * 1024` is a module constant (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:24). `truncateOutput` (subagent-tool.ts:171-178) compares `Buffer.byteLength(text,'utf8')` against it, walks the slice back a character at a time, and returns `${truncated}\n\n[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` — no file is written and no path appears. Its only call site is the model-facing body in `contentForResults` (subagent-tool.ts:236, header at :227, called once from the tool's result assembly). `createSubagentTool`'s options (subagent-tool.ts:75-92, wired at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1470-1483) carry `getCwd`/`getDepth`/`getMaxParallelTasks` but NO session path, so the tool has nowhere to spill even if it wanted to — unlike `createWorkflowTool` (index.ts:1495 `getSessionPath: () => generationConfig.sessionPath`) and `createWebFetchTool` (index.ts:1395), which both write session-dir files. No env override exists under any spelling: `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` has zero non-doc hits repo-wide (`grep -arn`, so NUL-byte files were not skipped) and there is no `NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`, although the file that would own it already exists and already maps four Claude env names to `NESSY_*` ones (packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:8-12) and is already imported by this very tool (subagent-tool.ts:5). The overflow is not immediately discarded but the fallback is weaker than the doc's: the inline text comes from `completed.result ?? completed.output` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:628) after a `monitor` read that the host bounds to `MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:42, applied by `boundResult`/`toResult` at :585-607), and the only retrieval handle, `get_subagent_result(agent_id)` (subagent-tool.ts:688-715), bounds to `DEFAULT_RESULT_BYTES = 16 * 1024` unless the model passes `verbose: true` (child-session-service.ts:43, :275-278) — i.e. 16 KiB, HALF of what the truncated inline block already showed. The untruncated text does survive host-side: SessionManager writes the child's last assistant message into the record unbounded (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:9998 `return { status: 'completed', output, result: output, ... }`), and `PiChildSessionStateV1` is persisted (child-session-service.ts:536), so the bound is a read-side projection, not a capture-side loss. Nothing tests any of this: `grep -arln 'truncateOutput|Output truncated' --include=*.test.ts packages` returns nothing.
divergence: Not a key-name-only mismatch — one of the three obligations is entirely absent and the other two are wrong in value and in unit. (1) DISK SPILL: absent. The doc requires the full output on disk and its path inside the truncated response; we write no file and the marker is a bare `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` (subagent-tool.ts:177). The parent's only recourse is `get_subagent_result(agent_id)`, which is not the documented mechanism and by default returns 16 KiB — less than it already had. (2) TUNABILITY: absent. `OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES` is a hardcoded constant; `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` (and any `NESSY_*` analogue) is unread, so the documented 160000 ceiling is unreachable. (3) UNIT: we count UTF-8 BYTES (32768) where the doc counts CHARACTERS (32000). ASCII output is near-parity (32768 vs 32000 chars, ours slightly larger); two-byte text — Cyrillic, which is this fork's primary locale — is cut at ~16 384 characters, roughly half the documented budget, and CJK/emoji worse. A separate consequence of the same fixed number: even if the cap became tunable, values above 64 KiB would do nothing, because the host's read-side `MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (child-session-service.ts:42) is what the inline path receives.

change.what: Add `export function resolveTaskMaxOutputChars(env: EnvRecord = process.env): number` reading `NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH`: parse base-10 integer, clamp to [1, 160_000], and fall back to 32_000 when unset/non-numeric/<=0 — mirroring the doc's default and maximum exactly. This file is the established home: its header (:8-12) is already the `CLAUDE_* → NESSY_*` mapping table, so add the row `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH → NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` with the env-vars.md:425 quote, and reuse the module's existing `EnvRecord` type and default-`process.env` convention.

Delete `OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES` and count characters: `const cap = resolveTaskMaxOutputChars()` (import from '../../../shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts' — the same relative import already on :5), compare `text.length`, slice `text.slice(0, cap)`, and drop the byte-walk loop (character slicing cannot split a code point; keep a lone-surrogate guard if the last unit is a high surrogate). Give `truncateOutput` a spill: change the signature to `truncateOutput(text: string, ctx: { agent: string; agentId?: string; sessionPath?: string })`, and when over cap write the PRE-truncation text with `mkdirSync`/`writeFileSync` from 'node:fs' (same imports workflow-tool.ts:8 uses) to `<sessionPath>/long_responses/<ISO-timestamp>_subagent_<safeAgentName>.txt` — the canonical folder (`LONG_RESPONSES_DIR`, packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts:48) that the system prompt already teaches the model to read (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:1044). Marker becomes `[Output truncated to <cap> characters for the parent context. Full output: <absolutePath>]`; on missing session path or a write failure fall back to today's bare marker plus the `get_subagent_result(agent_id, verbose:true)` hint, never throw. Add `getSessionPath?: () => string | undefined` to `CreateSubagentToolOptions` and thread it to the single call site at :236 (`contentForResults` needs the option object or a resolved path parameter). Do NOT touch the tool's description/schema/promptSnippet: `hashProjectedPiToolDefinition` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/harness/tool-manifest.ts:365-379) hashes exactly those, and the pins live at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts:44 (`subagent`) and :51 (`subagent:fork-mode`).
One added line: `getSessionPath: () => generationConfig.sessionPath,` — literally the same expression `createWorkflowTool` already receives at :1495.

Required only if the documented 160000-character maximum must actually be reachable and 'full output' must mean full. Today the inline path can never see more than 64 KiB and `get_subagent_result` no more than 16 KiB, so a raised cap is inert above 64 KiB. Two options: (a) raise `MAX_RESULT_BYTES` to at least the byte cost of 160000 characters and raise `DEFAULT_RESULT_BYTES` to the resolved cap so the retrieval handle is never narrower than the inline block; or (b) preferred for fidelity — spill HOST-side, where the untruncated text still exists (SessionManager.ts:9998 stores it unbounded on the record), and carry the written path as a new optional field on `PiChildResult` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts, `getResult` signature at :151) so the subprocess names the host's file instead of re-writing a bounded copy. Option (b) is a wire + persistence change; option (a) grows persisted `PiChildSessionStateV1` records.

change.what: Nothing currently covers `truncateOutput` at all. Add: (1) over-cap case with a temp session path — asserts the marker contains the absolute path AND that reading that file back yields the pre-truncation text byte-for-byte; (2) under-cap pass-through — unchanged text, no file created; (3) env cases — `NESSY_TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=100` cuts at 100 characters, `=999999` clamps to 160000, garbage falls back to 32000; (4) a Cyrillic string of 20000 characters must NOT be truncated at the 32000 default (the byte-vs-character regression guard). Set/restore the env inside the test — several suites in this repo mutate module-scope env, and two concurrent `bun test` processes manufacture failures.

blastRadius: Contained to the Pi orchestrator's subagent result path if the change stops at items 1-3. `truncateOutput` has exactly one caller (`contentForResults`, subagent-tool.ts:236) and `contentForResults` exactly one caller inside the same file; both are reported by codegraph as having no covering tests. Sibling symbols that must NOT be touched: `truncateOutput` in packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:27 (`MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 20_000`, a different subsystem), `contentForResult` in workflow-tool.ts:327, and the workflow sandbox's `maxOutputBytes` (orchestrator/sandbox.ts:28). Model-contract surface: safe only while the tool's name/description/schema/promptSnippet/promptGuidelines stay identical — those five are what `hashProjectedPiToolDefinition` (harness/tool-manifest.ts:365-379) hashes, checked at extensions/guard.ts:86 and harness/tool-manifest.ts:292-293 against the pins in harness-tool-descriptor.ts:44 and :51; touching the description means re-pinning BOTH `subagent` and `subagent:fork-mode`, and packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts pins source ranges in this file too. Adding the env resolver to background-task-settings.ts touches a module imported by pi-agent.ts:201, local-tools/runtime.ts:4, index.ts:82, subagent-tool.ts:5 and spawner.ts:6 — additive export only, no existing behaviour changes. Item 4 explicitly crosses boundaries: `MAX_RESULT_BYTES` is exported and reused by SessionManager.ts:131/9940 for partial-output recovery (the comment at child-session-service.ts:37-41 says the two must bound with the SAME number), the child records it bounds are PERSISTED via `options.persist` (child-session-service.ts:536), and adding a path field to `PiChildResult` changes a subprocess↔host WIRE type in shared/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts. Both of those are risk triggers in this repo. Files written under `<sessionPath>/long_responses/` also fall inside session retention sweeps (packages/shared/src/sessions/retention-sweep.ts:23, storage.ts:96), so spilled files are cleaned up with the session rather than leaking.
userImpact: Observable today whenever a subagent returns more than ~32 KB — routine for the research/audit/review subagents this repo itself dispatches. The parent model receives the first 32768 bytes plus `[Output truncated to 32KB for the parent context.]` and nothing else: no file path, no instruction, and its only recovery call (`get_subagent_result(agent_id)`) hands back 16 KiB unless it happens to pass `verbose: true`, so a naive retry makes the parent's view SMALLER. The user sees the orchestrator summarise or act on a partial subagent report — and because the details payload keeps the untruncated (≤64 KiB) text (subagent-tool.ts:215 `text: result.text`, carried to the host through packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts), the subagent card in the UI can show text the model never saw, which reads as 'the agent ignored its own subagent'. For Russian-language work the cut arrives at roughly 16 000 characters instead of the documented 32 000, so it bites at half the length a Claude user would expect. And a user who follows Claude's docs and exports `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=160000` gets no effect at all — the value is never read.
notes: Effort M covers items 1-3 plus tests (character-counted, env-tunable cap and a real spill of the text the subprocess holds). Item 4 is what makes the documented 160000-character maximum and the literal word 'full' true; taken on, it crosses server-core plus a shared wire type and is L on its own.
